newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen 50 cts-$1 up, Brent flat/5cts down.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen 50 cts-$1 up, Brent flat/5cts down.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures should open 50 cents to $1 a tonne firmer on Thursday after reports of another Turkish incursion into northern Iraq gave Brent a lift in late Wednesday trade, dealers said.
"Brent recovered very well last night, partly in response to the Turkish story, so that should help gas oil this morning," said one.
IPE June gas oil closed $1.50 lower at $176.25 a tonne on Wednesday, missing out on the late bounce provided by reports of rising tension on the borders of the Kurdish enclave in northern Iraq.
Turkish troops have pushed 200 km into northern Iraq in a nine-day border offensive against Kurdish guerrillas, Iraqi Kurdish officials said on Thursday.

Turkey's operation in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) separatists has unnerved its neighbours. Turkey's state-run news agency Anatolia reported Wednesday that Iraq, Syria and Iran have all built up forces in the region.
IPE Brent crude closed 13 cents firmer at $20.13 a barrel, reversing losses posted when an early rally inspired by mildly supportive U.S. inventory data ran out of steam.

"The Turkish incursions are still causing a few jitters but basically you have two schools of thought: the fundamentalists think the market should be coming lower but then there are a lot of long funds who are happy to sit with it," said a broker.

Dealers saw interim support on Brent at $20.00 a barrel. Gas oil, meanwhile, was stuck in the middle of a $175-$180 a tonne trading range with little momentum seen for break in either direction, dealers said.
The approach of a long holiday weekend in Britain and the U.S. was expected to keep markets thin and choppy, they said.
